title: Seniorský spôsob práce
tags: senior úsudok rozhodovanie judgment ownership autonomy
use: Use when starting any task covered by this skill. Senior behavior means making proportionate, defensible decisions and owning the outcome through verification. It does not mean pretending to know missing facts or claiming every professional specialty.
decision: Identify the requested outcome, existing authorization, source of truth, constraints and highest consequential uncertainty. Separate a reversible local choice from an external commitment. Use a one-sentence decision for a small edit; use a short architecture record when several teams, data or costly dependencies are affected. Make routine choices and continue. Ask only for a missing fact or decision that materially changes scope, irreversible action or correctness, after completing independent work.
deliverable: Provide the completed change, why the key choice fits, actual verification, remaining material limits and the next owner where needed. Maintain a concise decision trail, not a document bureaucracy. Apply this contract to every selected chapter, including legacy chapters.
acceptance: Choose checks from actual failure consequences. A screenshot cannot prove checkout; unit tests cannot prove visual polish; a checklist cannot certify accessibility. Keep blocked checks explicit and finish what remains authorized. Fix the important observed defect before adding another effect. Stop optional work once the requested outcome and relevant checks are satisfied.

title: Kompletný produkčný postup
tags: Kompletný produkčný postup production playbook
use: Complete website workflow
decision: Choose a complete functional slice before multiplying visual effects.
deliverable: A working visitor journey and coherent composition.
acceptance: Inspect the real primary action with mobile and failure behavior.

title: Riadenie produkcie
tags: Riadenie produkcie studio operating system
use: Scope routing and implementation slices
decision: Scale process to the actual request and isolate the weakest assumption.
deliverable: A scoped plan and reviewable vertical slices.
acceptance: Observe each slice before propagating its pattern.

title: Rozsah, rozpočet a hodnota
tags: Rozsah, rozpočet a hodnota scope and value
use: Budget and value planning
decision: Translate the user's price ambition into explicit outcomes and assumptions.
deliverable: A bounded scope with effort and recurring-cost assumptions.
acceptance: Check required inputs and do not represent illustrative prices as market evidence.

title: Discovery a overiteľné požiadavky
tags: brief zadanie requirements discovery
use: Use when a brief names a style, price or technology without describing the visitor's task. Resolve known context before asking the user to repeat it.
decision: Identify who uses the site, what action matters and what evidence must precede that action. Classify a request as a feature, quality attribute, constraint or preference. “Cinematic” is a visual intention; “booking survives a failed video load” is an acceptance condition. Record assumptions with consequences rather than filling gaps with invented facts.
deliverable: Produce a brief containing the visitor job, verified facts, requirements, constraints, unknowns, scope boundary and acceptance examples. Keep the brief as short as the project permits; discovery is complete when it enables responsible execution, not when every imaginable question has been asked.
acceptance: Walk the proposed journey using supplied facts. Check that each required feature has a content/data owner and a check. If a missing backend prevents confirmation, label that dependency instead of promising a real submission. Challenge conflicting requirements: a large interactive simulation on a tight mobile budget needs a fallback or narrower scope.

title: Odhad práce a kompromisy
tags: odhad hodiny budget tradeoff estimate
use: Use when choosing a scope, comparing production options or explaining cost. Treat prices in this skill as user-requested planning scenarios, not market valuations.
decision: Estimate the work required for an outcome, not the number of sections or effects. Distinguish a predictable implementation from an uncertain integration or missing media production. Compare a still image, pre-rendered shot and interactive scene by visitor benefit, production effort, runtime cost and future editing.
deliverable: Return a bounded scope, assumptions, effort range, recurring costs, excluded work and a condition for revising the estimate. Recommend one option and explain the tradeoff. Save actual effort lessons only when there is reliable project evidence; never manufacture historical estimates or a return on investment.
acceptance: Check that review, correction, integration failure paths and handoff are included. Compare the proposed first slice with the available time and actual team capability. Do not translate a €400,000 ambition into an automatic enterprise stack or a €1,500 budget into an unsupported promise of custom 3D commerce.

title: Architektonické rozhodnutia
tags: ADR architecture stack architektura server client
use: Use when a choice changes responsibility boundaries, deployment, data authority or long-term cost. Skip a formal record for routine local styling.
decision: Start with the existing system and its real limits. Compare retaining it, extending it and replacing it against the required journey, operating skill and migration risk. Choose by constraints rather than novelty. Distinguish a reversible library choice from a content model or identity scheme that will be costly to migrate.
deliverable: Provide the decision record and the minimum component/data diagram needed to understand it. Include a migration or exit path for meaningful lock-in. Keep rejected options brief and factual. Revisit the decision when its stated constraint changes; do not endlessly reopen it because a different framework becomes popular.
acceptance: Ask whether the proposed choice can be built, operated and changed by the actual maintainer. Check dependency compatibility and implementation documentation at the installed versions. Exercise one costly boundary, such as authenticated data caching or editor preview. A successful isolated demo does not settle production availability or integration concerns.

title: Komunikácia a zmeny rozsahu
tags: stakeholder revisions scope change komunikacia
use: Use when several people influence the result or new requests change agreed work. Keep this proportional to project size and existing authorization.
decision: Identify who owns business truth, design direction, technical acceptance and release. Distinguish a correction to agreed behavior from additional scope. An inaccessible booking button is a defect; adding subscriptions may be a new product requirement. Do not use change control as an excuse to avoid routine fixes.
deliverable: Produce a short decision/update record suitable for the recipient. Use plain language and real observations, not “premium” as an explanation. For a solo small website, a few lines can carry the entire record. For a programme, preserve traceability across work packages without turning every spacing change into a committee decision.
acceptance: Before handing off, compare the implemented behavior with accepted requirements and the latest steering. Ensure unresolved decisions have an owner and impact, not just a vague “TBD”. Verify that users can inspect the thing they are being asked to approve; do preparatory work before a real release confirmation is needed.

title: Riziká a závislosti projektu
tags: risk dependency blocker kriticka cesta
use: Use when missing inputs, integration uncertainty or release constraints can derail execution. Treat uncertainty as something to resolve, not a reason to stop all work.
decision: Identify the small set of risks that could invalidate scope, create irreversible damage or break the visitor's primary task. Describe each as cause, event and consequence. Separate an actual blocker from a preference and from a future hypothetical concern. Give priority to high consequence and weak evidence.
deliverable: Keep a compact risk/dependency register and a next-action list. Mark resolved risks with the observation that resolved them. Report only material remaining limitations to the user. Do not add a generic safety checklist to a low-impact design edit; senior judgment includes keeping effort and caution proportionate.
acceptance: At each useful milestone check whether the original assumption still holds. Reassess only affected risks after changes. Make sure mitigation actually reduces the consequence rather than creating a new fragile dependency. An untested backup is not verified recovery; a disabled button is not duplicate transaction protection.

title: Výber nástrojov a schopností
tags: Výber nástrojov a schopností tool routing
use: Tool selection and limits
decision: Use existing purpose-built capabilities and verify actual availability.
deliverable: A justified tool path with a usable fallback.
acceptance: Check current APIs and never infer installation from a catalog entry.

title: Analýza referencií a prenos princípov
tags: references research referencia inspiracia
use: Use when learning from a website, image or video reference. A reference should answer a design question, not dictate the entire finished site.
decision: Select complementary references for composition, motion and functional structure. State the visitor need each informs. Record whether evidence comes from a static image, video, live interaction, source code or documentation. A still cannot establish easing, reverse scroll or mobile behavior.
deliverable: Provide a small evidence board: source, evidence class, useful mechanism, proposed adaptation and limitation. Load the existing W/FX catalogs selectively. Do not claim that cataloging 100 examples means all their code, live behavior or business results have been validated.
acceptance: Compare the adaptation with actual content and device constraints. Reject references that require unavailable imagery or bury the user's core action. Check one stable frame without animation: weak hierarchy is not repaired by a dramatic transition. Mark uninspected reference conditions explicitly.

title: Práca s katalógmi
tags: Práca s katalógmi catalog guide
use: Catalog lookup and evidence classes
decision: Select a few relevant records and preserve their evidence class.
deliverable: A bounded set of references and concrete proposed adaptations.
acceptance: Separate observed behavior from static preview and proposed reconstruction.

title: Metódy odvodené z referencií
tags: Metódy odvodené z referencií learned methods
use: Applying researched composition methods
decision: Transfer a principle that serves the actual visitor rather than copying a whole identity.
deliverable: An original application tied to the content.
acceptance: Inspect whether the selected method fits available media and interaction constraints.

title: Detailné prompty a zadania pre dizajnéra
name_sk: Detailné prompty a zadania pre dizajnéra
tags: Detailné prompty a zadania pre dizajnéra prompt adaptation grafik grafika grafického dizajnéra graphic designer prompt prompty detailed
use: Designer briefs and prompt adaptation
decision: Resolve real inputs, select the task prompt and demand inspectable deliverables.
deliverable: A complete scoped designer prompt with composition, states and handoff.
acceptance: Check factual truth, missing inputs, mobile variants and acceptance criteria before use.

title: Pôvod zdrojov a hranice dôkazov
tags: Pôvod zdrojov a hranice dôkazov provenance
use: Sources, rights and claims
decision: Keep source claims, original proposals and runtime observations distinct.
deliverable: A traceable source and evidence record.
acceptance: Do not inflate catalog coverage, test scope or commercial value.

title: Umelecký smer a filmový scenár
tags: Umelecký smer a filmový scenár art direction
use: Brand story and composition
decision: Choose a visual relationship that communicates the business story.
deliverable: A still composition and purposeful scene plan.
acceptance: Evaluate real copy, crop and primary action before animation.

title: Vizuálne alternatívy a kritika
tags: Vizuálne alternatívy a kritika visual direction review
use: Distinctive options and composition review
decision: Compare genuinely different compositions against the visitor job.
deliverable: A selected direction with observed corrections.
acceptance: Do not invent comparison scores when no baseline was inspected.

title: Značka a jednotný vizuálny systém
tags: brand identity znacka visual system
use: Use when the site needs a recognizable identity or several surfaces must feel coherent. Work from the real brand assets and audience rather than a default luxury aesthetic.
decision: Define a few observable traits: editorial or utilitarian typography, intimate or expansive crop, quiet or energetic motion, precise or organic geometry. Tie each to the business and actual media. Avoid treating black backgrounds, gold accents and oversized serif text as universal signals of quality.
deliverable: Supply a concise visual contract, token mapping, approved examples and source asset references. Specify which decisions are system rules and which are page-specific compositions. Do not force every section into identical cards merely to claim consistency; consistency concerns relationships and behavior, not uniformity of every layout.
acceptance: Review the same content across desktop, mobile, loading, error and CMS edge cases. Ensure identity survives when a hero video is unavailable. Check whether buttons and links remain identifiable without the accent color. A distinctive site should still be legible when the decorative layer is removed.

title: Texty, ponuka a dôveryhodnosť
tags: copy content texty claims social proof
use: Use when the offer is vague, the interface depends on invented filler or important claims lack support. Treat copy as part of the functional design.
decision: Identify the visitor's question at each stage: what is offered, whom it suits, what it includes, what it costs and how to proceed. Match claims to an authorized source. Distinguish an aspiration, a fact, an estimate and a testimonial. Do not convert uncertainty into a confident marketing number.
deliverable: Provide final copy with a fact/source map for consequential claims, unresolved factual dependencies and editable placement. Use a content hierarchy rather than a wall of slogans. Record who maintains changeable details such as hours, services and prices so a polished launch does not immediately become misleading.
acceptance: Read the page as a first-time visitor and follow each action. Check that text remains true when media fails, translated copy expands or the provider changes availability. Compare labels with the actual form or external booking step. “Book now” should not secretly be an unprocessed email request.

title: Publikum a pozícia produktu
tags: audience positioning persona user research
use: Use when several possible customers or product stories compete for attention. Keep research claims separate from assumptions about an audience.
decision: Choose the primary visitor job and the situation that brings that visitor to the site. Distinguish a new prospect, returning customer, editor and account administrator. They may share a brand but need different information and interaction speed. Do not invent demographic precision unsupported by actual research.
deliverable: Provide a short positioning statement, evidence-backed priorities, assumptions and the content consequences. Recommend one direction with its tradeoff. Define what new information would change the decision. Avoid manufacturing personas that add detail without changing what the team builds.
acceptance: Walk the proposed page for at least the primary and one materially different visitor. Check whether the same CTA wording means different things to them. Use direct user feedback where available; do not present your own preferences as validated audience research. Evaluate clarity before speculative persuasion tactics.

title: Informačná architektúra
tags: IA sitemap hierarchy struktura navigacia
use: Use when content is difficult to find or a redesign changes page structure. Start from user questions and content ownership, not a fashionable section order.
decision: Choose what belongs on one page, what needs its own address and which information must be available before a decision. Separate public discovery from authenticated work. A long scroll is appropriate only if the sequence clarifies a story; essential comparison or reference material may need direct access.
deliverable: Provide the page/content map, primary journeys, navigation labels and redirect needs. Link to the relevant CMS schema and SEO plan when those are in scope. Avoid expanding a small business page into dozens of thin pages purely to increase the apparent project size.
acceptance: Walk representative find-and-act tasks from search, a deep link and the homepage. Check that no important answer exists only inside a hover, canvas or unavailable video. Test navigation on a narrow viewport and with keyboard focus. Compare old and new URL coverage before migration.

title: Používateľská cesta a konverzia
tags: UX journey funnel rezervacia conversion
use: Use when a visitor can admire the site but cannot confidently complete its purpose. Define conversion by a real outcome rather than animation completion.
decision: Choose a primary action and the evidence needed before it. Distinguish intent, submission, accepted operation and fulfilled service. Decide which steps are essential and which are avoidable friction. Respect the user's autonomy; clarity is more durable than deceptive urgency.
deliverable: Provide the journey map, actual destinations, state model, event meanings and observed checks. Report friction and uncertainty as findings, not unmeasured conversion uplift. If comparing alternatives, define the behavioral hypothesis and evidence needed before declaring a winner.
acceptance: Complete the journey from a cold load, direct link and mobile viewport. Exercise one realistic interruption or rejection. Confirm that apparent success follows an authoritative response and that a second click cannot accidentally duplicate a consequential operation. Inspect whether the UI still works with decoration disabled.

title: Typografia a fonty
tags: typography font pismo diakritika text
use: Use when type hierarchy, readability or font loading limits the design. Treat the font file, license and language coverage as production inputs.
decision: Choose roles before families: display, body, interface, numeric data and occasional accent. Select contrast in scale, weight and rhythm that suits the actual copy. Avoid using many families to manufacture identity. Confirm Slovak glyphs and any required scripts from real files or authorized previews.
deliverable: Supply role tokens, responsive ranges, font sources/licenses, loading strategy and examples. Record any intentional display treatment that must not spread to forms or paragraphs. Use the designer typography prompt when commissioning alternatives; require real text and a fallback specimen, not only a title on an empty board.
acceptance: Inspect long Slovak titles, accents, numerals, zoom, font failure and narrow viewports. Compare the first paint with the final font. Check overflow and readability in dense UI as well as the hero. Review actual contrast and focus; beautiful letterforms alone do not establish accessibility.

title: Mriežka, proporcie a kompozícia
tags: grid layout mriezka whitespace spacing
use: Use when a page feels generic, crowded or unstable across content lengths. Build a system of relationships rather than a sequence of identical boxes.
decision: Choose the dominant element and the supporting reading path for each section. Set container width, gutters, alignment anchors and spacing rhythm. Let content determine where asymmetry helps. Reserve intentional exceptions for meaningful visual emphasis.
deliverable: Provide layout constraints, alignment rules, responsive transitions and content resilience examples. A designer handoff should explain what stretches, wraps, stays fixed or changes order. Do not deliver only fixed desktop pixels and expect the developer to invent all intermediate behavior.
acceptance: Resize between the designed widths, not just at the endpoints. Exercise one/many items, long labels, missing imagery and text enlargement. Check accidental overflow, overlapping layers and focus obstruction. Inspect still frames at the start, middle and end of animated layouts.

title: Farby, kontrast a stavové významy
tags: color colour palette kontrast farba accessibility
use: Use when a palette must carry both identity and usable information. Distinguish decorative color from semantic state and interaction.
decision: Assign roles for surfaces, primary/secondary text, borders, actions, focus, success, warning and error. Choose hierarchy before adding gradients. A single brand accent need not carry every status. Define the actual foreground/background pairs to evaluate.
deliverable: Supply semantic palette tokens, allowed pairings, status conventions and observed contrast results. State unresolved media combinations. Use designer briefs to request evidence on real components rather than an attractive palette swatch alone. Do not claim a full accessibility pass from color checks.
acceptance: Measure relevant contrast pairs using the applicable current accessibility criteria; use S022 for criterion context. Check focus against adjacent surfaces and all interactive states. Inspect actual composited frames and media fallback. A static token value cannot prove a changing background is always readable.

title: Dizajnové tokeny a komponenty
tags: tokens components design system variant Figma
use: Use when repeated UI needs to stay consistent or a handoff must survive future change. Scale the system to actual reuse.
decision: Separate primitive values, semantic roles and component-specific decisions. Choose component boundaries by behavior and ownership, not visual resemblance alone. Two cards that look similar may have different semantics; one button may require several well-defined states.
deliverable: Provide the token map, component inventory, state matrix, usage examples and ownership. Include only useful abstractions; a small landing page may need a handful. Use the designer system prompt for a complete reviewable package, including developer naming and editable source structure.
acceptance: Place components in representative dense, sparse, narrow and error contexts. Exercise keyboard behavior, long labels and disabled/loading states. Check that a token change improves the intended surfaces without altering unrelated semantics. Compare design variants with the code contract and flag missing states.

title: Kompozície jednotlivých sekcií
tags: Kompozície jednotlivých sekcií section recipes
use: Hero, service, proof, pricing and booking sections
decision: Match layout to the information a section must communicate.
deliverable: Content-specific responsive sections.
acceptance: Check long text, missing optional media and actual CTA destination.

title: Formuláre a validácia
tags: forms formular field error validation
use: Use when the site accepts user input, including contact, booking, checkout or CMS editing. Keep input collection proportional to the real task.
decision: Specify why each field is needed, which system validates it and when an operation is confirmed. Distinguish required, optional and conditionally required data. Prefer native controls with familiar behavior unless a specialized control has a defensible benefit.
deliverable: Provide field/schema contracts, validation timing, error messages, state designs and actual submission evidence. S051 supplies accessible form principles; provider-specific validation and transaction rules must be checked for the selected backend. Do not use a synthetic success response as proof of a working live form.
acceptance: Use keyboard entry, pasted values, missing/invalid input, slow response and server rejection. Check that errors identify the affected field and can be found without color. Exercise mobile keyboard obstruction and return to an earlier step. A required field silently hidden by a responsive layout is a release defect.

title: Navigácia a vyhľadávacie rozhranie
tags: menu navigation search nav vyhladavanie
use: Use when visitors need to move between pages or find items. Keep orientation available while decorative scenes change.
decision: Choose a small visible navigation structure matching information architecture. Use search when there is enough content and a real retrieval mechanism to justify it. Distinguish page navigation, in-page jumps, filters and application actions; they need different semantics.
deliverable: Supply navigation structure, state rules, focus behavior and query/URL contracts. For large data use the separate search/data chapter. Do not add an ornamental search field that has no real index or useful results just to fill a header design.
acceptance: Test direct links, keyboard traversal, escape where appropriate, browser Back and narrow screens. Check that animated overlays never remain as invisible click interceptors. Try a long query, no match and delayed response. Validate the actual destination rather than only the visual menu opening.

title: Odolnosť dizajnu voči obsahu
tags: edge cases content overflow long text CMS
use: Use when a composition must survive editing, localization and missing optional media. Treat real variability as a design input.
decision: Identify which content is required for meaning and which is optional decoration. Set constraints based on the domain rather than convenient placeholder length. Decide how absence, unknown, zero and unavailable differ; do not collapse them into an empty string.
deliverable: Provide supported content rules, fallback compositions and a few reusable fixtures. Record which constraints the CMS enforces and which the UI handles. A professional template should remain usable after an ordinary editorial change without requiring a developer to retune every animation.
acceptance: Render fixtures at representative widths and inspect the actual result. Check text zoom, sorting, filtering and animated reorder. Confirm that a missing optional field does not create a mysterious gap or disable the main action. Test data validation separately from presentation behavior.

title: Jazyk a plynulosť pohybu
tags: Jazyk a plynulosť pohybu motion language
use: Timing, easing and motion ownership
decision: Choose purposeful motion with one authority per changing property.
deliverable: A motion contract with interruption and fallback.
acceptance: Observe reverse input, preference change and cleanup.

title: Filmové a webové prechody
tags: Filmové a webové prechody cinematic transitions
use: Cuts, masks, morphs and continuity
decision: Choose a transition that preserves meaning and spatial orientation.
deliverable: Transition phases with stable frames and state ownership.
acceptance: Check interruption, reverse, transformed layouts and unsupported capability.

title: Kontinuita scén a kamery
tags: Kontinuita scén a kamery scene continuity
use: Scene partitions and resource adoption
decision: Keep text, camera and selected state coherent across time and async completion.
deliverable: A deterministic scene/state plan and ownership rules.
acceptance: Exercise mid-page entry, out-of-order loads and disposal of unclaimed resources.

title: Storyboard a animatik webu
tags: storyboard animatic film scenar shot
use: Use when a cinematic sequence is too complex to judge from a moodboard. Treat the web as an interactive document with controllable pacing.
decision: Give each scene one visitor question and one visual answer. Choose the entry, readable hold and exit. Decide whether time, scroll or explicit interaction owns progress. Do not combine independent clocks without a synchronization contract.
deliverable: Provide frame names, progress/time boundaries, copy, shot notes, layer ownership, media needs and fallback. Use the detailed designer storyboard prompt to commission this package. Distinguish a visual proposal from an executed animation; hand off the logic that connects frames, not only attractive endpoints.
acceptance: Inspect start, overlap, hold and exit frames. Check that subject identity, reading order and action remain clear when the user pauses between planned beats. Test the proposed transition direction against the spatial relationship it implies. Flag impossible crops or missing imagery before implementation.

title: Easing, časovanie a fyzika pohybu
tags: easing spring timing damping duration rychlost
use: Use when animation feels abrupt, floaty, mechanical or inconsistent. Diagnose timing and property ownership before adding blur.
decision: Choose the movement's purpose: immediate feedback, spatial continuity, emphasis or narrative pacing. Use duration-based motion for repeatable editorial choreography and spring behavior when direct manipulation should settle naturally. Do not prescribe one duration for every travel distance or context.
deliverable: Provide motion tokens with purpose, parameter meaning and tested conditions. Keep suggested values as starting hypotheses until observed in the actual composition. If a numerical easing choice is changed, describe its perceptual effect rather than claiming a specific curve makes every interface premium.
acceptance: Observe rapid repeated input, interruption halfway, reverse scroll and background/foreground return. Inspect settled state after cancellation. Compare at different refresh rates when practical; a single recording cannot establish consistent frame pacing. Use reduced-motion changes at runtime as an ownership test.

title: Filmové rozprávanie pri skrolovaní
tags: scroll scrollytelling pin sticky scrub chapters
use: Use when sequential explanation benefits from a changing visual scene. Preserve the document's navigation and the user's control over pace.
decision: Choose between ordinary sections, sticky composition and a bounded pinned sequence. Pin only when a stable stage improves comprehension. Define a skip/direct-link path and the text equivalent. Avoid converting the whole website into one mandatory intro.
deliverable: Supply chapter boundaries, state mapping, measurement dependencies, ownership, cleanup and fallback. Link the scene-plan template and relevant FX records. A smooth recording is only one observation; document reverse, mid-page and reduced-motion behavior separately when they have actually been checked.
acceptance: Reload halfway through, scroll upward, jump via anchor, resize and use Back. Try a short viewport and rapid wheel/touch input. Confirm the CTA is usable while assets load or fail. Profile the actual scene before increasing pin duration or adding more passes.

title: Zdieľané prvky a prechody stránok
tags: shared element route view transition FLIP navigation
use: Use when continuity across layouts or pages helps orientation. Keep navigation state authoritative and animation optional.
decision: Choose whether the object truly represents the same entity in both states. Use stable identity, not a coincidental index. Decide whether a native transition, framework layout system or measured FLIP fits the installed environment. Check feature-specific support instead of assuming a universal API.
deliverable: Provide shared IDs, route ownership, request cancellation semantics, focus/scroll rules and fallback. Keep transition-specific concerns isolated so removing the effect does not break the product. Record which lifecycle branches were tested with mocks and which were observed in a browser.
acceptance: Exercise two rapid navigations, Back during transition, a failed data load, reduced-motion changes and route unmount. Confirm no duplicate commit, stale focus jump or invisible overlay remains. Test unsupported transition capability with ordinary navigation still working.

title: Mikrointerakcie a spätná väzba
tags: hover press loading feedback microinteraction
use: Use when controls feel unresponsive or state changes are difficult to perceive. Favor meaningful feedback over decorative activity.
decision: Identify the user's intent and the system's actual state. Distinguish hover, focus, pressed, selected, busy, successful and failed. Avoid using one visual change to imply both selection and server confirmation.
deliverable: Supply a control-state matrix, transition purpose, timing, input equivalents and server/UI boundary. Do not attach sound, particles or celebration to every click. A well-designed microinteraction makes the state easier to understand and leaves the visitor in control.
acceptance: Test hover-to-click, focus-to-Enter, touch, cancellation and failed response. Observe a low-power or reduced-motion path. Check that disabled controls explain what is required where that is not obvious. Ensure visual success never fires before the actual accepted outcome.

title: Filmová typografia a kinetický text
tags: kinetic typography text split reveal titulky
use: Use when text itself carries a narrative beat. Preserve comprehension and semantic content while adding movement.
decision: Choose a small phrase worth emphasis and a motion metaphor connected to its meaning. Distinguish an editorial title from instructions, pricing or legal conditions that should stay stable. Decide whether a line reveal, mask, scale or position change is enough.
deliverable: Provide text, typography roles, line-wrap strategy, transition phases and semantic/fallback treatment. Designer prompts must ask for complete stable frames and mobile behavior, not only a spectacular title animation. Remove the effect if it delays comprehension or makes the main action harder to find.
acceptance: Pause mid-reveal, resize, fail the font load and change the motion preference. Check that a user entering the section halfway can still read the full meaning. Verify copy/paste and accessible naming where appropriate. Inspect contrast over changing imagery at each meaningful frame.

title: Zvuk a ovládanie médií
tags: audio sound video playback mute subtitles
use: Use when a site includes video, narration or optional sound design. Make audio an intentional user choice.
decision: Classify media as decorative, explanatory or essential content. Decide which information needs captions, a transcript or another accessible equivalent. A decorative loop should not become the only source of instructions or product facts.
deliverable: Provide media purpose, source rights, formats, poster, controls, alternatives and observed playback checks. Consult the chosen provider's current implementation guidance for exact behavior. Do not promise universal autoplay or a cinematic audio experience without the user's explicit interaction.
acceptance: Try rejected playback, network failure, tab suspension, sound disabled, keyboard controls and reduced motion. Check that captions are readable and do not cover the main action. An audio J/L cut is a film editing technique; a silent web overlap is an analogy, not proof of sound continuity.

title: Kamera a príprava 3D scény
tags: Kamera a príprava 3D scény camera and assets
use: Camera paths and media preparation
decision: Choose the least costly medium that gives the needed control.
deliverable: Shot plan, asset requirements and renderer assumptions.
acceptance: Inspect subject framing, path continuity and mobile alternatives.

title: VFX a compositing
tags: VFX a compositing vfx compositing
use: Shaders, bloom, fog, grading and effect chains
decision: Select a compatible renderer pipeline and justify each pass.
deliverable: Bounded effect chain with controllable quality.
acceptance: Check color output, overdraw, context failure and no-effect baseline.

title: Produkcia a výkon médií
tags: Produkcia a výkon médií asset performance pipeline
use: Decoded memory and asset optimization
decision: Budget transfer, decoding and residency separately.
deliverable: Versioned derivatives and a nominal memory plan.
acceptance: Compare actual appearance and measured cost under stated conditions.

title: Svetlo a materiály v 3D
tags: lighting material PBR svetlo render
use: Use when a 3D scene looks flat, artificial or inconsistent with the brand. Solve lighting and material response before adding post-processing.
decision: Choose the subject, silhouette and visual hierarchy. Decide whether realistic product representation or stylized illustration is required. Keep product colors, proportions and finishes truthful when they support a purchase decision.
deliverable: Provide lighting intention, material slots, color-management assumptions, source assets, quality tiers and comparison frames. Keep editable values understandable to another developer. Consult renderer-specific sources S010–S012 before adapting code; WebGL and WebGPU effect pipelines are not interchangeable.
acceptance: Inspect bright and dark views, camera movement, low-quality fallback and the final compositing chain. Check for blown highlights, crushed details, incorrect normals, z-fighting and unreadable product markings. Compare a real product reference where truth matters. Do not infer physical accuracy from visual appeal alone.

title: Výroba a ladenie shaderov
tags: shader GLSL TSL uniform GPU fragment
use: Use when a visual mechanism genuinely requires per-pixel or per-vertex computation. A shader is an implementation choice, not a requirement for a premium site.
decision: Define the visual relationship and input domain first: UV, object/world position, screen coordinates, pointer or progress. Choose the renderer and shader language compatible with the existing project. Prefer a simpler mask or pre-rendered asset when it communicates equally well.
deliverable: Provide parameter contract, coordinate spaces, renderer/version, cost drivers, disposal responsibility and a static fallback. Preserve source/license for adapted algorithms. Use current official TSL or renderer documentation, and label illustrative pseudocode as such instead of presenting incompatible snippets as ready to run.
acceptance: Test boundary values, resize, high/low pixel ratio, missing textures, fallback renderer and reduced motion. Inspect output with post-processing disabled to isolate faults. Profile the actual workload before claiming optimization. A shader compiling in one environment does not establish device coverage.

title: Častice a simulácia
tags: particles simulation noise physics GPU
use: Use when motion of many elements helps express a material, system or story. Do not use particles to disguise weak composition.
decision: Choose deterministic analytic motion for a reversible scroll narrative and stateful simulation only when its behavior matters. Define bounds, density, visual purpose and which input affects it. Decide what happens when the tab sleeps or the user jumps to another chapter.
deliverable: Provide state model, timestep/seed policy, boundaries, quality controls, lifecycle ownership and the observed performance conditions. Keep a stable poster or CSS alternative. Do not claim physical realism or universal frame rate from an aesthetically convincing desktop preview.
acceptance: Measure steady state, first appearance, rapid input, long runtime and background return. Check for unbounded buffers, orphaned loops and inconsistent resets. Compare reduced-motion and no-GPU alternatives. Ensure pointer interaction never captures scrolling or hides accessible controls.

title: Optimalizácia modelov a LOD
tags: glTF model LOD mesh textures compression
use: Use when models load slowly, exceed memory budgets or render poorly on target devices. Optimize the asset for its actual camera use.
decision: Inspect geometry, draw calls, materials, texture dimensions, animation tracks and useful viewing distance. Choose which details affect silhouette or identity. A small transfer size is not evidence of low decoded memory or cheap rendering.
deliverable: Provide original/derivative mapping, chosen transformations, visual comparison, nominal memory estimate and measured device results where available. Use S016 and S041 for tool/disposal context. Do not describe an offline estimate as a real GPU measurement or delete the editable master after producing a web derivative.
acceptance: Compare original and optimized versions in representative close, distant and mobile shots. Inspect UV seams, normals, labels, transparency and animation. Measure transfer, decode, upload and steady-state separately. Repeat mount/replace/unmount to detect ownership problems.

title: Video a obrazové sekvencie
tags: video sequence frames codec poster scroll
use: Use when a fixed cinematic shot can replace expensive runtime 3D or when a sequence explains a process. Choose the medium by control and resource needs.
decision: Compare video, stills, a bounded image sequence and interactive rendering. Video often suits timed playback; image sequences can support precise frame selection but consume decoded memory. Define the needed frame accuracy and fallback before choosing.
deliverable: Provide source/export settings, frame count, loading window, nominal memory inputs, progress mapping and fallback. State actual observed playback/device coverage. A beautiful MP4 export proves the shot's appearance, not the website's scroll performance.
acceptance: Test cold load, rapid reverse, jump to the end, narrow crop, decode failure and memory pressure. Check the seam if looping and inspect the poster when playback never starts. Keep real copy and actions in DOM throughout.

title: Práva a autenticita podkladov
tags: rights licensing media authenticity fotky prava
use: Use when selecting photographs, video, models, fonts, illustrations or generated imagery. Preserve truth and traceable origin without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.
decision: Classify assets as real business evidence, licensed illustration, generated concept or placeholder. Use authentic media for actual premises, people, products and services unless the user explicitly requests a clearly understood transformation. Do not silently turn a generated scene into a claimed customer result.
deliverable: Provide an asset manifest, source/derivative relationship, credits and unresolved rights dependencies. Keep originals replaceable. Never assume generated imagery guarantees exclusivity or legal clearance; report what the actual tool/license and authorized inputs establish.
acceptance: Compare final assets with originals for unwanted alterations, misleading before/after claims and lost credits. Check whether fonts, stock or model licenses cover the planned delivery. Inspect alt text and captions for invented identities or unsupported context.

title: Adaptívna kvalita a náhradné zobrazenie
tags: adaptive rendering fallback quality WebGL WebGPU
use: Use when one visual scene must serve different hardware, preferences and network conditions. Plan graceful alternatives before failure occurs.
decision: Define a useful base experience in semantic DOM, then optional visual tiers. Choose degradation in a meaningful order: expensive post effects, resolution, particle/detail density, then a stable poster where needed. Do not use device names as a substitute for capability and observation.
deliverable: Provide tier criteria, resources per tier, transition behavior, fallback composition and observed coverage. Record which capability branches are code-reviewed versus runtime tested. Avoid a “premium only” route that leaves visitors with an empty canvas or an endless loader.
acceptance: Exercise unsupported API, failed asset load, context loss where tooling permits, slow network, reduced motion and a quality downgrade mid-scene. Check that state does not reset or diverge from the DOM. Observe memory and responsiveness after repeated tier changes.

title: Implementačné recepty pohybu
tags: Implementačné recepty pohybu implementation recipes
use: CSS, WAAPI, GSAP and motion runtimes
decision: Use a scoped mechanism compatible with the current stack.
deliverable: An integrated effect with lifecycle and fallback.
acceptance: Distinguish utility test results from browser rendering evidence.

title: Framework a stratégia renderovania
tags: SSR SSG SPA hydration framework server
use: Use when a new project needs a stack or an existing render path causes a concrete problem. Preserve a viable existing stack.
decision: Classify public content, personalized data, editor preview and highly interactive surfaces. Choose static, server or client rendering per real requirement rather than applying one mode everywhere. Consider hosting constraints, content freshness, team knowledge and the cost of hydration.
deliverable: Provide route/rendering decisions, data ownership, deployment assumptions and a reproducible build path. Explain why any new dependency is necessary. Do not claim that a framework alone guarantees SEO, performance or maintainability; those outcomes depend on the implemented path.
acceptance: Run the actual build and inspect cold entry, direct routes, server errors and client navigation. Check that a missing optional bundle does not remove the main content. Measure loading/hydration costs before rewriting architecture. Verify APIs against installed versions and current official docs.

title: Komponenty a vlastníctvo stavu
tags: component state ownership props reducer
use: Use when state becomes inconsistent or a component mixes unrelated responsibilities. Split by behavior and ownership rather than file-size anxiety.
decision: Identify authoritative domain state, derived presentation state, transient interaction state and external resources. Decide the narrowest owner that can coordinate consumers correctly. Avoid maintaining several independently editable copies of selected variant, price or route.
deliverable: Provide the state owner map, component contracts, allowed transitions and important invariants. Include cleanup ownership for external resources. Favor a few clear seams over a general-purpose abstraction that makes ordinary changes harder to understand.
acceptance: Exercise state combinations that must be impossible: unavailable product marked purchasable, old model with new price, success after failed submission. Check repeated mounts and changed props. Validate external data at the boundary rather than relying on static types alone.

title: Životný cyklus a uvoľňovanie zdrojov
tags: lifecycle cleanup dispose memory leak ownership
use: Use when animations, subscriptions, models or buffers survive their intended scope. Establish ownership before adding cleanup calls.
decision: For every resource identify creator, owner, borrowers, lifetime and release operation. Shared textures and caches need an explicit sharing policy; blindly traversing a removed object and disposing everything can break other scenes. Distinguish a suspended page from a permanently unmounted component.
deliverable: Provide an ownership table, lifecycle rules, observed repetition results and remaining GPU/browser gaps. Code-level disposal tests prove control flow, not that every driver released memory. Never fix a leak by removing a necessary ownership guard without understanding who still uses the object.
acceptance: Repeat mount, replace, cancel and unmount. Exercise late completion and cleanup errors without disposing the new owner's value. Track resource counts and memory under stated conditions; retained renderer caches can differ from a genuine leak. Check Back/forward restoration separately from ordinary unmount.

title: Súbeh, asynchrónne operácie a transakcie
tags: async race cancellation latest transaction idempotency
use: Use when requests can overlap, responses arrive late or repeated intent has consequences. Reads, writes and owned-resource loads need different contracts.
decision: Use latest-wins for replaceable reads such as search or preview selection. Use explicit transaction/idempotency rules for writes such as booking and payment. Aborting local presentation is not proof a server operation was cancelled. Define what “cancel” actually means for each boundary.
deliverable: Provide operation identities, state transitions, retry/reconciliation rules and ownership of late results. Record provider versions and bounded test evidence. The bundled latest-resource utility coordinates reads; it is not a general payment or database transaction system.
acceptance: Force out-of-order success, stale error, duplicate intent, timeout after accepted write and unmount before completion. Assert the final authoritative state and user-visible recovery. Test retry handling against the real integration contract in an authorized test environment; a mocked animation callback is not enough.

title: URL, história a priame odkazy
tags: URL history back forward deep link router
use: Use when meaningful state should survive reload, sharing or browser navigation. Let the established router own history.
decision: Choose which state belongs in a path/query/hash and which is ephemeral. Product identity, filters and a meaningful chapter often merit a URL; pointer position usually does not. Keep sensitive data out of URLs because they may appear in logs and referrers.
deliverable: Provide the URL schema, push/replace rules, parsing behavior, title/focus/scroll policy and observed navigation checks. Use established routing APIs at installed versions. Do not build a second global popstate handler without reconciling it with the existing router.
acceptance: Open a direct link in a fresh session, reload, change filters, navigate away and return. Test malformed/unknown parameters and browser Back during a pending route. Check whether a restored scroll position agrees with the cinematic scene's computed state.

title: Mobilná kompozícia a dotyk
tags: mobile responsive touch safe area viewport
use: Use whenever the website must work beyond the desktop artboard. Mobile is a composition and interaction decision, not a scaled screenshot.
decision: Choose the essential subject, message and action at narrow widths. Decide which desktop relationships reflow, simplify or become sequential. Remove hover dependencies and excessive camera travel. Preserve the full visitor task even if the visual technique changes.
deliverable: Provide mobile composition, crop rules, responsive transitions, input behavior and quality/fallback tiers. Require mobile states in designer briefs before final desktop polish. A handoff is incomplete if it leaves every narrow-screen decision to improvisation during coding.
acceptance: Inspect intermediate widths, orientation changes, keyboard-open forms, long copy and reduced motion. Check sticky overlays, bottom controls and focus visibility. Separate responsive emulation from actual physical-device observations in the evidence. Do not claim all mobile devices from one screenshot.

title: Schopnosti prehliadača a progresívne vylepšenie
tags: capability feature detection browser progressive enhancement
use: Use when relying on modern CSS, transition, media or graphics features. Build a useful base and add capability-specific behavior.
decision: Identify the exact feature the design needs, not merely an API family name. Decide the fallback for unsupported behavior and partial failure. Browser brand or a successful constructor does not prove every required subfeature works.
deliverable: Provide a capability matrix, base/enhanced behavior and evidence for the tested environments. State version-specific uncertainty where relevant. A fallback should be an intentional design with the same primary purpose, not an error message telling visitors to buy a different device.
acceptance: Exercise unsupported branches deliberately instead of waiting for a user report. Test a rejected initializer, missing chunk, reduced motion and fallback navigation. Inspect the baseline with decorative JavaScript unavailable. Do not infer performance from feature detection.

title: Odolné rozhranie a obnova po chybe
name_sk: Odolné rozhranie a obnova po chybe
tags: error recovery empty offline retry resilience
use: Use when normal network, content or dependency failures can leave the visitor stuck. Design recovery as part of the main flow.
decision: Distinguish empty data, unavailable service, forbidden access, invalid input, stale data and unexpected failure. Decide which failures can be retried safely and which need reconciliation or another route. Avoid a generic “Something went wrong” for every condition.
deliverable: Provide the error taxonomy, user messages, retry/reconciliation policy and observed checks. Avoid inventing backend behavior to make a mockup look complete. Report a blocked integration honestly while finishing the rest of the authorized experience.
acceptance: Simulate the specific failures that threaten the primary journey. Check focus, messages, preserved input and actual recovery. Return from another route after an error and repeat the action. Confirm that failures do not expose secrets, raw customer data or misleading success states.

title: Závislosti a reprodukovateľný build
tags: dependency lockfile packages build version license
use: Use when adding packages, upgrading a stack or preparing a maintainable handoff. Every dependency becomes part of the operating cost.
decision: Inspect the existing package manager, lockfile and scripts. Add a library only for a demonstrated need that justifies bundle, maintenance and compatibility costs. Prefer one coherent motion/rendering authority over overlapping libraries performing the same job.
deliverable: Provide dependency rationale, lockfile changes, build evidence and any upgrade limitations. Remove unused experiments and temporary packages. Do not treat the skill's catalog of 100 tools as an instruction to install them or as evidence that they are already available.
acceptance: Run the relevant build and targeted checks from the actual project. Inspect changed dependency/lockfile scope and investigate unexpected churn. Confirm that documented start/build commands are real. A passing type check does not establish runtime library compatibility or visual quality.

title: Kontrakty obsahu a integrácií
tags: Kontrakty obsahu a integrácií content and integration contracts
use: Editable data and honest provider states
decision: Keep content, identity and authoritative integration outcomes aligned.
deliverable: Schemas, stable mappings and real failure states.
acceptance: Check unpublished content, reordered entries and provider rejection.

title: CMS a redakčný pracovný postup
tags: CMS editor draft preview publish schema
use: Use when non-developers must maintain content. Design the editing experience alongside the public website.
decision: Identify editors, content types, approval needs, locales and publication frequency. Choose structured content for meaningful entities and bounded composition controls where editorial flexibility is useful. Do not make editors manage shader uniforms or raw layout CSS for routine changes.
deliverable: Provide the schema, role/permission map, publishing sequence, content fixtures and short editing instructions. Record which operations were actually exercised. A static content JSON file is not a complete CMS merely because the frontend reads it dynamically.
acceptance: Have the authorized editor workflow create, update, reorder, preview and unpublish representative content in a test context. Exercise long text, missing optional media, conflicting edits and invalid references. Check that draft data cannot appear through a public cache or unauthenticated preview link.

title: API kontrakty a validácia dát
tags: API schema validation version pagination error
use: Use when the website consumes or exposes external data. Treat every boundary as a contract with independent failure modes.
decision: Define request identity, permitted inputs, response shape, error semantics, pagination and version expectations. Distinguish trusted internal invariants from unvalidated external values. Static TypeScript types do not validate network responses.
deliverable: Provide schema, mapping, failure/retry behavior, version assumptions and representative fixtures. Mark which fields are display-only versus authoritative. Do not silently coerce corrupt data into plausible business values just to prevent an error screen.
acceptance: Test a valid response, missing required data, unknown enum, malformed value, empty page, rate limit and provider failure. Inspect whether errors retain enough safe context for diagnosis without leaking secrets. Exercise the real authorized provider path for integration evidence, not only synthetic fixtures.

title: Dátový model a migrácie
tags: database migration schema transaction rollback
use: Use when persistent data structures change. Start from domain invariants and the compatibility needs of running code.
decision: Identify entities, relationships, identity, uniqueness, required history and deletion semantics. Decide which invariants belong in constraints or transactions. Separate an additive compatible change from a destructive conversion; authorization to adjust a UI does not automatically authorize deleting production data.
deliverable: Provide migration steps, preconditions, backup/restore path, compatibility window, verification and owner. Keep unknown data quality visible until measured. A successful migration script exit is insufficient evidence that business relationships were preserved.
acceptance: Test on representative authorized fixtures including duplicates, missing values and interrupted batches. Check row/entity counts and important invariants before and after. Verify old/new application behavior during the transition and inspect query plans for affected hot paths. Do not run destructive production experiments to prove the design.

title: Identita a oprávnenia
tags: auth session authorization RBAC tenant permissions
use: Use when users access private data or privileged actions. Treat identity and permission as separate concerns.
decision: Choose an established identity solution suitable for the project. Map actor, resource, action and context, including tenant boundaries. Default-deny sensitive operations and define how permissions are checked at the authoritative server boundary. Hiding a button is presentation, not enforcement.
deliverable: Provide the permission matrix, provider/version assumptions, session lifecycle, safe failure states and bounded evidence. Apply a relevant security skill for material review. Do not claim certification or complete security from a short checklist.
acceptance: Use authorized test accounts for two distinct users/tenants. Try direct resource access, stale sessions, changed roles and protected downloads. Verify server denial rather than only absence of UI. Test the most consequential permission boundary before claiming an authenticated flow is complete.

title: Rezervácie a dostupnosť
tags: booking reservation slot availability timezone
use: Use when users choose a service, time, resource or practitioner. An available-looking calendar is not a reservation system.
decision: Identify the authoritative provider, slot duration, location timezone, resource constraints and confirmation rules. Distinguish external-link booking, embedded provider flow and custom server integration. Do not infer live availability from a static schedule.
deliverable: Provide integration type, state model, authoritative IDs, timezone policy and actual evidence. If the scope is a real external link, report that honestly. Do not call a decorative date picker or synthetic confirmation a working booking integration.
acceptance: Use an authorized test environment or read-only destination check appropriate to scope. Test unavailable slots, expired selection, slow response, repeated submit and return from the provider. Check daylight-saving and locale formatting for the actual location. Avoid sending real customer notifications merely to test a design.

title: Obchod, ceny a checkout
tags: commerce SKU variant pricing cart checkout payment
use: Use when visual product choices affect what a visitor buys. Keep commerce authority separate from scene presentation.
decision: Identify catalog, SKU/variant identity, currency, price/tax source, inventory and payment provider. Distinguish displayed estimate from authoritative charge. Choose provider-supported checkout patterns before building a custom transaction interface.
deliverable: Provide catalog mappings, authority boundaries, state/error flow and tested provider path. Use the appropriate commerce/payment skills for concrete integration work. Keep business policies and jurisdiction-specific requirements sourced; do not invent refund, tax or shipping conditions.
acceptance: Exercise selection changes during loading, unavailable variants, quantity bounds, currency formatting, rejected payment and duplicate webhook/retry paths in the authorized test context. Confirm the order/charge corresponds to the selected real SKU. A polished success screen is not evidence of successful payment.

title: Webhooky a úlohy na pozadí
tags: webhook queue retry deduplication background job
use: Use when external events or slow work update the system asynchronously. Design for duplicates, delay and out-of-order delivery.
decision: Define event identity, authenticated origin, durable receipt, processing state and side effects. Distinguish receiving an event from completing its business action. Choose a queue only when asynchronous work and operational needs justify it.
deliverable: Provide event contracts, deduplication scope, processing states, retry/replay procedure and ownership. Record limitations honestly. Do not describe an in-memory Set as durable duplicate protection for a multi-instance production system.
acceptance: Test invalid signature, duplicate event, delayed older event, worker crash and replay. Confirm the business invariant rather than just HTTP status. Check that failure logs contain useful identifiers without secrets or unnecessary customer payloads. Exercise the real provider's authorized test delivery where available.

title: Lokalizácia, mena a čas
tags: locale i18n Slovak timezone Bratislava DST
use: Use when content, money or schedules serve multiple languages or regions. Locale and timezone are different inputs.
decision: Identify supported languages, authoritative timezone, currency and translation owner. Distinguish an instant, a local date and a recurring wall-clock appointment. Never assume the execution server's timezone is the user's or business's timezone.
deliverable: Provide locale/time/currency policy, content ownership, URL strategy and representative fixtures. Use current formatting API documentation and actual provider semantics. A translated heading does not make an otherwise hardcoded booking or checkout flow fully localized.
acceptance: Inspect Slovak diacritics, long translations, numeric formatting and screen-reader labels. Test daylight-saving boundaries relevant to the business, direct localized links and missing translation. Compare server/client rendering to prevent mismatched formatted output on hydration.

title: Vyhľadávanie a veľké dáta
tags: search indexing pagination virtualized large data
use: Use when visitors navigate a substantial catalog or administrators work with many records. Optimize the real query and task, not a synthetic row count.
decision: Define searchable fields, ranking intent, filters, authorization, freshness and expected scale. Choose client-side search only when payload and privacy permit it. Distinguish server pagination from UI virtualization; they solve different costs.
deliverable: Provide query/index contracts, pagination, selection identity, freshness and accessibility behavior. Record measured conditions and scale assumptions. Do not add a search engine or infinite scroll to a small content site without a real visitor benefit.
acceptance: Test no results, many results, changing filters quickly, late responses, deleted records and permission changes. Check duplicate/missing items at page boundaries. Measure actual payload, rendering and query behavior under representative data; a mocked list is not load testing.

title: Výkon a prístupnosť v praxi
tags: Výkon a prístupnosť v praxi performance accessibility
use: Mobile, runtime cost and accessibility
decision: Protect the primary task while choosing visual cost.
deliverable: A usable mobile/reduced-motion/failure experience.
acceptance: Measure actual bottlenecks and inspect meaningful accessibility paths.

title: Načítanie a Core Web Vitals
tags: LCP INP CLS loading preload lazy performance
use: Use when the useful page appears late, interaction lags or layout jumps. Diagnose the actual critical path before changing visual quality.
decision: Identify the likely main content, first action and large layout shifts. Distinguish lab observations from field experience and preserve the measurement conditions. Choose loading priorities around visitor usefulness rather than treating every decorative asset as urgent.
deliverable: Provide the bottleneck, targeted change, observed result, measurement method and remaining uncertainty. Treat numeric budgets as project decisions and public thresholds as sourced definitions. A perfect synthetic score is not proof of reliable bookings, accessible navigation or real-world performance.
acceptance: Record cold and warm paths with explicit device/network/tool settings. Inspect LCP, INP and CLS according to current definitions and field context. Test the actual primary interaction, not only initial load. Compare before/after under comparable conditions and avoid interpreting a single noisy run as a guaranteed improvement.

title: Profilovanie runtime a pamäte
tags: profiling trace FPS memory leak GPU CPU
use: Use when motion stutters, a scene slows over time or resource use grows. Measure before selecting an optimization.
decision: Choose a reproducible action and identify whether the suspected bottleneck is network, decode, main-thread JavaScript, layout/paint, GPU or memory pressure. Frame rate alone does not identify the cause. Distinguish persistent growth from expected caches and temporary peaks.
deliverable: Provide the trace/observation, environment, diagnosis, correction and bounded comparison. Do not claim universal 60 fps or device coverage from local utility tests. Keep an actionable next step when the evidence does not yet distinguish CPU from GPU cost.
acceptance: Repeat the same scenario after the change and inspect unintended visual/functional differences. Test long-session behavior only where a real risk exists. Confirm that a “fix” did not merely hide the scene or disable necessary interaction. Mark browser/GPU checks blocked if the environment cannot perform them.

title: Klávesnica, fokus a dialógy
tags: keyboard focus dialog modal escape tab
use: Use when controls, overlays or route transitions affect keyboard navigation. Focus is part of application state, not decorative styling.
decision: Choose native control semantics and determine whether an overlay is truly modal. Define opening focus, traversal, escape/close behavior and return focus. Nonmodal menus and panels should not trap focus as if they were dialogs.
deliverable: Provide focus rules, keyboard behaviors, selected pattern and actual manual observations. Use S026 and S036 for scoped criteria/pattern guidance. Do not claim full accessibility from a working Tab key or from an ARIA attribute added without corresponding behavior.
acceptance: Complete the main journey with keyboard only. Open/close overlays, trigger validation, navigate Back and activate skip links. Check focus after the original trigger is removed. Inspect both visual visibility and programmatic location. Automated tooling can help but cannot establish the entire interaction.

title: Sémantika a čítačky obrazovky
tags: semantic screen reader headings alt ARIA
use: Use when the visual experience relies on canvas, split text, icons or rich custom controls. Preserve a coherent nonvisual representation.
decision: Identify meaningful content, decorative media, controls and status changes. Choose native HTML before custom roles. Decide what information the visual scene conveys and provide an equivalent path without duplicating every decorative object in the accessibility tree.
deliverable: Provide semantic structure, media alternatives, status-announcement policy and observed coverage. Keep gaps explicit. A cinematic site can remain expressive while offering the same meaningful information and actions through a conventional document.
acceptance: Inspect the accessibility tree and, when tools permit, perform representative screen-reader tasks with a named browser/reader combination. Check control names, headings, error discovery, changing status and route context. A source review or automated scan is only partial evidence.

title: Obmedzený pohyb a zmyslová prístupnosť
tags: reduced motion vestibular flashing pause sensory
use: Use whenever animation, autoplay or flashing could affect comfort or comprehension. Reduced motion changes the experience's motion behavior, not its usefulness.
decision: Classify effects as essential to a task or decorative. Choose a stable alternative for parallax, large camera travel, rapid scaling and endless loops. Check applicable criterion levels and conditions; do not conflate all motion guidance into a claim of automatic conformance.
deliverable: Provide an effect-by-effect alternative and control policy. State which accessibility checks were performed and which remain open. User comfort is a design constraint from the beginning, not a stylesheet appended after the final demo.
acceptance: Test the preference at initial load and during an active transition, including reverse scroll and route changes. Check that cancellation does not leave opacity zero or invisible click blockers. Inspect pause state, resumed state and static media fallback. Record actual conditions tested.

title: Bezpečnosť webovej aplikácie
tags: security XSS CSRF secrets upload authorization
use: Use when the project handles input, identities, uploads, sensitive data or third-party integrations. Apply controls to actual trust boundaries.
decision: Identify assets, actors, entry points and consequential failure paths. Select a risk-appropriate verification scope and relevant specialist skill. A public brochure and a multitenant payment portal need different depth; neither benefits from unsupported certification language.
deliverable: Provide the addressed risks, controls, evidence and remaining material issues. Do not promise the site is unhackable or fully secure. Security work should result in concrete verified behavior, not a generic warning that prevents an otherwise authorized low-risk edit.
acceptance: Exercise the affected authorization/input boundaries in an authorized test context. Check denial paths as well as successful access. Review error/log output for exposure. Use targeted tests and scans as evidence for their actual scope; investigate findings rather than blindly suppressing them.

title: Súkromie, súhlas a minimum dát
tags: privacy consent cookies personal data retention
use: Use when forms, analytics, embeds or accounts process personal information. Start from the actual data flow and jurisdiction.
decision: List what is collected, why, where it goes, who can access it and how long it remains. Distinguish necessary product operation from optional analytics/marketing. Determine which legal or policy decisions require current authoritative guidance rather than assumptions.
deliverable: Provide the data-flow map, implemented controls, policy dependencies and observed tests. Browse current official sources for specific legal guidance and route consequential legal interpretation appropriately. Keep this chapter as engineering procedure, not a jurisdiction-independent legal certificate.
acceptance: Inspect network behavior before and after the relevant preference, including reload and return visits. Check forms and events for unnecessary identifiers. Verify access to stored records and the documented retention/deletion path in an authorized test environment where applicable.

title: Cache a konzistentnosť dát
tags: cache CDN invalidation stale private consistency
use: Use when content freshness, performance or privacy depends on cached responses. Make cache identity and authority explicit.
decision: Classify immutable assets, public changing content, personalized data and transactional truth. Choose freshness tolerance for each. A cached product description may be acceptable while cached availability cannot authorize a new reservation. Define who invalidates or revalidates after a change.
deliverable: Provide cache classes, keys, lifetimes, invalidation triggers and evidence. Do not apply one aggressive policy to every response to improve a benchmark. Performance and consistency must both match the visitor task.
acceptance: Test cold/warm reads, content update, logout/account change, locale change and stale provider response. Inspect actual headers and returned data through the deployed path. Confirm that invalidation reaches the user-visible layer and does not leak another visitor's data.

title: Offline stav a životný cyklus prehliadača
name_sk: Offline stav a životný cyklus prehliadača
tags: offline reconnect bfcache pagehide pageshow lifecycle
use: Use when tab suspension, disconnection or Back/forward restoration can break the experience. A page may pause and resume without a fresh mount.
decision: Choose which read-only information may remain useful offline and which actions require authoritative connectivity. Do not queue consequential writes unless the product has explicit operation identity, reconciliation and user expectations. Separate transient suspension from permanent teardown.
deliverable: Provide lifecycle states, pause/resume ownership, offline boundaries and recovery behavior. Mark browser checks separately from mocked events. Preserve the primary task even if the cinematic layer must return as a still frame.
acceptance: Test away/Back, tab suspension, network loss during read/write and restoration with stale data. Check that animation time does not jump through seconds of queued work. Record whether restoration actually used BFCache; pressing Back alone does not prove it.

title: Brány kvality
tags: Brány kvality quality gates
use: Acceptance before delivery
decision: Do not let visual appeal compensate for broken truth or functionality.
deliverable: A scoped acceptance result with unresolved limitations.
acceptance: Verify relevant gates and keep unexecuted checks unpassed.

title: Revízia a diagnostika
tags: Revízia a diagnostika review and debug
use: Observed faults and targeted correction
decision: Isolate the cause of the most consequential observed failure.
deliverable: A reproducible diagnosis and correction.
acceptance: Recheck the affected path rather than broadening tests without a reason.

title: Dôkazy a akceptácia
tags: Dôkazy a akceptácia evidence and acceptance
use: Build-linked evidence records
decision: Select methods that can establish the actual claim.
deliverable: A build-linked evidence ledger.
acceptance: Treat record consistency as consistency, not authentication or certification.

title: Vizuálna kontrola a regresie
tags: visual regression screenshot art direction critique
use: Use when implementation may drift from an approved composition or a change affects multiple layouts. Combine measurable regression checks with visual judgment.
decision: Select representative pages, states and viewports based on the changed risk. Distinguish unintended regression from an intentional redesign. A pixel difference is evidence of change, not automatically a defect; a similar screenshot is not proof of good design.
deliverable: Provide representative captures, concise findings, corrections and residual limitations. For designer critique use the detailed review prompt and require concrete locations, reasons and changes. Never invent a before score or claim a visual improvement was measured when no comparable baseline exists.
acceptance: Use the supported browser/design tools for actual capture. Keep blocked visual checks explicit; source reading or Node tests do not replace them. Inspect mobile and real-content variants instead of relying solely on an ideal desktop screenshot. Record what a human/agent actually observed.

title: Integračné a end-to-end testy
tags: integration E2E testing transaction user journey
use: Use when independently correct pieces can fail together. Choose tests that protect meaningful behavior and boundary contracts.
decision: Identify the few failures with real consequences: wrong SKU, duplicate booking, unauthorized data, lost form input or inaccessible navigation. Choose the narrowest test layer that can reveal each. Avoid brittle tests that mirror implementation or add ceremony to trivial reversible changes.
deliverable: Provide scope, environment, commands/observations, results and remaining gaps. A passing local suite is evidence for those cases only. Preserve useful regression tests for observed bugs and avoid inflating quality claims by counting superficial assertions.
acceptance: Investigate flaky failures rather than masking them with arbitrary waits or repeated passes. Assert outcomes and invariants, not CSS selectors chosen only because they are convenient. Re-run affected tests after fixes and stop broader repetition once the concrete risk is resolved.

title: Testovanie prístupnosti
tags: accessibility testing WCAG audit keyboard reader
use: Use when accepting a user-facing flow or changing semantics, focus, contrast or motion. Match evidence to the claimed scope.
decision: Choose relevant pages, states, content variations and applicable criteria. Distinguish automated findings, manual interaction checks and specialist conformance review. A broad compliance claim needs broader evidence than this skill's routine checks.
deliverable: Provide tested scope, findings by user impact, fixes, unresolved issues and evidence limits. Reference current standards for precise requirements. Do not average away a blocked primary task because the rest of the page looks excellent or because an automated scanner reported no errors.
acceptance: Recheck the specific issue after correction and ensure the fix did not damage another input mode. A removed focus outline may make a screenshot cleaner while making navigation worse. Mark blocked assistive-technology/device checks honestly and continue independent work.

title: Výkonnostné rozpočty a regresie
tags: performance budget regression bytes memory frame
use: Use when cinematic ambition must fit device, loading or operating constraints. Budgets are explicit project decisions backed by observation.
decision: Choose budgets for the useful first view, interaction responsiveness, media transfer, retained memory and runtime work that matter to the project. Tie each to a user/device scenario. Do not use one universal megabyte or frame-rate limit as proof of quality.
deliverable: Provide budgets, rationale, observed measurements, tradeoffs and accepted exceptions with owner. Make the next developer able to reproduce the useful check. A budget spreadsheet without real traces or observations is a planning artifact, not performance validation.
